mechanism.baseline: An inherited construction makes the 55-byte and 63-byte last chunks agree on chaining-value words 0,2,5,7. For equal prefixes and a common chunk counter, complete agreement on all eight chaining words gives a complete-message collision. The initial half equality alone is not a full collision.
mechanism.counter_walk: For one member, t_hi=s XOR KS with KS the low 16 bits of ROL(K1.d1,16). Then K1.a1=(K0r-KS)+s while X0 and w3 decrease by one as s increases. Across 2^16 steps, X0's upper half changes at most once, creating at most two blocks. Within a block the low half of E=omega is fixed.
mechanism.typed_relation: For member type t=Y4[4] XOR Y4[5], necessary test-(2) witness relations are f[9] XOR f[10]=1 and f[24] XOR f[25]=1 XOR t. The member class has 262144 members of each type. Typed carry automata reject impossible low-half blocks and index lists of accepted upper halves for live blocks.
mechanism.list_selection: The upper-half mapping from X0's low half is an XOR with a fixed half-word followed by a fixed modular addition. An interval decomposes into at most 16 aligned binary intervals. XOR preserves each aligned interval as an interval; addition introduces at most one wrap across the disjoint images, giving at most 17 ordinary ranges. Prefix-count tables select exact slices of sorted accepted-high-half lists. Seven 36-bit entries fit a 256-bit word. This skips rejected steps rather than scanning them.
mechanism.solver_boundary: List acceptance is a necessary existential projection of J2, not a collision certificate. The eventual root h must satisfy J1, J2 and J3 with the same witness f=ROR(y XOR (Q+h),12); subsequent screening and capped solving remain necessary.
